title: One name per thing: a glossary in every repo
why: Your idea, Oct 26: AI sessions need settled terms. A photos folder beside a captures folder leads to confusion, a second copy being built, and misread asks.
note: Checked Oct 26: no glossary in claude-settings (f463787), banchi (9683902) or home-app (65315da); q_max and home not checked. Only related rule: output-write-in-ste ('one term per meaning'), which covers prose, not names of folders, files, types or concepts. This is the naming side of o11 (one home per shared thing). Your word, Oct 26: agreed on GLOSSARY.md; claude-settings holds only terms that matter in every repo, each repo its own domain terms (a photos/captures clash is a repo row). Shape, advisor pick: (a) claude-settings GLOSSARY.md, pointed at from CLAUDE.md, not inlined: the workflow nouns (lane, batch, integration PR, worktree, handoff, step, ruling, decision, debt, guard, gate, owner, override pass and the like); (b) each repo's GLOSSARY.md, which never redefines a global term; (c) Plan, builder and reviewer check new names against both, and a small glossary skill seeds a repo's file; (d) a cheap CI check that each row's path exists and no new path uses a 'not:' name; (e) o2 puts the file in the shared layout. Third-party skills, advisor pick Oct 26: borrow from mattpocock/skills ubiquitous-language, credited, rather than install it. Main risk: a glossary written once goes stale; the CI check is the answer.
